proposals.relationship: Beard uses Tocqueville’s testimony about American women’s importance as a historical counterexample to Van Wyck Brooks’s marginal treatment of women in his account of early American literary and social life.
proposals.evidence_note: Own chapterIII P86–93criticizes Brooks’s1944WorldofWashingtonIrvingand explicitly invokes DemocracyinAmerica(1835/1840)atP92–93. This is a particular evidentiary resource, not agreement with Tocqueville’s entire gender theory or proof that every woman had equal power. Beard even allows the possibility of exaggerated French gallantry while pressing the contrast. Public transcription checked, original print and Tocqueville/Brooks books unread; no personal contact, mentorship or general school affiliation asserted.

proposals.relationship: Beard challenges the class-struggle formula she attributes to Marx when treated as a total explanation of history, arguing that it reduces human thought and action to material interests and leaves too little room for historical agency.
proposals.evidence_note: Own chapterXII P6responds directly to the CommunistManifesto’s formula;P3–7places it alongside other sweeping theories and immediately qualifies that the thinkers did not confine all their thought to these statements. The1848Manifestois jointly authored by Marx and Engels; Beard’s singular attribution does not establish sole authorship. This is her polemical reading, not an independently verified description of all Marx’s writings, every class analysis or her own coauthor Charles Beard’s views. Original Manifesto and print1946book unread; exact public primary transcription checked.

proposals.relationship: Beard criticizes Freudian literary interpretations that portray women chiefly as servants of male sexual drives and as neurotic, treating this as a reduction of women’s historical presence.
proposals.evidence_note: Own chapterIII P85explicitly targets literary circles governed by Freud’s doctrines. The endpoint is the Freudian-psychoanalysis grouping, not an assertion that Freud personally wrote every interpretation criticized or that all psychoanalytic work shares it. Her broad reception chronology and attributed Freud phrase are unverified source claims, not ours. P94–97separately reports Adler’s break and Beard’s objection to his individual-psychology remedy; Adler’s statements are not silently attributed to Freud or Beard. Original psychoanalytic works and whole1946print remain unread.
